mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings expectations and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of rising unemployment above 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 1.5% year-over-year signals deteriorating household demand, which reduces earnings growth and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of YoY RSAFS decline exceeding 1.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the industrial production index above 0.5% signals improving manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of monthly INDPRO increases above 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls above 100,000 coinciding with a monthly unemployment rate decline below 0.2 percentage points signals a tight labor market, which compresses profit margins and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 100,000 AND UNRATE falls < 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of strong payroll growth with falling unemployment below 0.2pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly federal funds rate above 4.5% combined with a monthly CPI inflation above 2.5% signals a restrictive monetary regime, which reduces consumer purchasing power and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of restrictive monetary policy with CPI > 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts above 10% year-over-year signals a sharp contraction in residential investment, which reduces GDP growth and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of YoY HOUST declines exceeding 10% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) below -2% year-over-year combined with a monthly GDP growth below 1% signals a deepening demand recession, which reduces earnings and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY < -2% AND GDPC1 YoY < 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of combined RSAFS and GDP declines meeting thresholds (t-test p > 0.05).
